plan: Hold workspace state as a plain-dict tree, deep-copied in __init__ and again in to_data() so external data can never alias internal state.
Drive total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline from one recursive (item, depth) generator so traversal order and nesting are defined in exactly one place.

Use precompiled regexes: strip markers matching \[\[\?(\w+)\]\] (replacing with a space) before counting words with \b\w+\b; notes contribute counted words and text markers, references contribute declared word_count and their unresolved list.
Render the outline as the workspace title plus one line per item, indented two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1), joined with newlines for determinism.

Implement move with a _locate helper returning (parent_list, index, item) and perform every validation — string-id type checks, item existence, destination existence, container kind, self/descendant containment via subtree scan, index bounds 0..len(destination) — before any mutation, so failed moves raise ValueError with to_data() unchanged.
Execute a successful move as delete-from-source then append or insert-at-index into destination, carrying the item subtree intact.
Collect unresolved marker identifiers into a set and return sorted(set) for uniqueness plus lexicographic order.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at construction and export (copy.deepcopy)
Single recursive document-order traversal generator shared by all read operations
Precompiled marker regex with strip-before-count word tallying
Parent-list locator returning (container list, index, item) for in-place list surgery
Validate-everything-before-mutate ordering guaranteeing atomic failed moves
Iterative subtree containment scan to reject self/descendant destinations
Set accumulation with sorted output for unique lexicographic marker identifiers
Kind-dispatched summary contributions (notes: counted text words; references: declared word_count)
